evidence: Ov. Met. 13.829–830: pars inde bibenda servātur
terms.comment: Traupman uses it for saving a file on a computer too.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with ad and the accusative, or the dative
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.224; Caes. BC 1.36 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to keep back, save up, qs. for future use; to reserve (very freq. and class.)”.
Lewis & Short: “to set apart, assign, appropriate, reserve, for any purpose”.

phrases.latin: lac mihi semper adest niveum: pars inde bibenda servātur, partem liquefacta coāgula dūrant
phrases.english: I always have snow-white milk: part of it is kept for drinking, part the rennet sets into cheese.
Save some of the cake for Dad.

sources: Lewis & Short: servo · Lewis & Short: reservo · Lewis & Short: sepono
